_comment: NIST ACVP vectors for ML-DSA-65 signature verification, from the
ACVP-Server repository, vector set 42.
Source:
gen-val/json-files/ML-DSA-sigVer-FIPS204/prompt.json
gen-val/json-files/ML-DSA-sigVer-FIPS204/expectedResults.json
SCOPE, and it is narrower than it looks.
Group 3 signs with a non-empty context string, and that is the only group
kept. It is also the only one that matters here, because it is the path
mili takes: the composite draft binds the ML-DSA half to the construction
by passing the algorithm label as ML-DSA's context string, so mili calls
verify_with_context with a thirty byte label. A verification vector with a
context exercises exactly that call.
Group 10 signs with an empty context, and its three cases that ACVP says
must verify do not verify through any FIPS 204 path in ml-dsa 0.1.1. They
are accepted by VerifyingKey::verify_internal, which the crate documents as
deliberately omitting the domain separator and the context boundary, so
verify_internal is not the algorithm FIPS 204 specifies and the ACVP
signatures do not match it either. verify_with_context with an empty
context is the specified algorithm -- it absorbs tr, a zero byte, a zero
length byte, then the message -- and it rejects them. The two readings of
the same vector disagree with each other, and the file does not record
which is right, so the three cases are left out rather than asserted either
way. `supply-chain/audits.toml` records the observation.
The consequence worth stating plainly: this file pins the context-aware
verification path against NIST, and pins nothing about empty-context
verification. mili has no exposure, because it never passes an empty
context -- LABEL is thirty bytes -- but a caller who reached for
verify_internal would get a verifier that disagrees with FIPS 204.
SELECTION. All three of group 3's positive cases are kept, plus four of
its negatives chosen for short messages, plus group 10's negatives. A
verifier test that only checks what must be accepted cannot show that
anything is refused, so the negatives are most of the file.
The `must_verify` field is ACVP's own verdict, not mili's. A false means
something was altered and verification must fail; ACVP does not record
what, so the test asserts the verdict and not a reason.
SIGNING is not covered. The sigGen groups give an expanded secret key rather
than a seed, and ml-dsa 0.1.1 reaches an expanded key only through
ExpandedSigningKey::from_expanded, which the crate deprecates and
documents as a panic risk. mili forbids panic paths, so consuming those
vectors would mean using the one entry point upstream tells callers not to.
mili's own signing output is pinned by the composite draft's Appendix E
vector in lamps19_composite_ed25519.json, which is a verification test too:
it carries the draft's key and message and checks that mili's signature
verifies under them.
